title: Psalm 91: In the Shadow of the Almighty
summary: The psalm describes the security of the one who dwells in the shelter of the Most High: God delivers him from the fowler's snare and the deadly plague, covers him with his wings, and commands his angels to guard him. Terrors by night and arrows by day will not overcome him, though thousands fall around him. In the closing lines God himself speaks, promising to deliver, answer, honor, and satisfy the one who loves him and knows his name.

from.where: The Study Bible's introduction to the Psalms
from.text: Psalms of trust rest in God's care (Psalms 23, 27, 91, 131).

line: The safety of the one who dwells in the shelter of the Most High, covered by his wings in plague and terror, ending with God's own promise to be with him in trouble.
guide: Pray it for real dangers, the surgery, the night shift, the long drive, but as trust and not as a charm; the shelter is a person. It is not a promise that no believer is ever harmed, and never a reason to refuse a doctor or ordinary care. Hold the promise of verse 15, God with you in trouble, whatever the outcome.

care.text: So this psalm is never a reason to refuse a doctor, medicine, or the ordinary care God also gives. Praying it and taking the medicine belong together.

If you have prayed this psalm over someone you have since lost, you did not pray wrong, and the one you lost was not loved less. In one chapter of Acts, “He had James, the brother of John, put to death with the sword” (Acts 12:2), while Peter was set free from prison. Acts never says that James had less faith. The context page on Psalm 91 says more about this.

stanzas.title: Dwelling in the shelter of the Most High
Protection from snare, plague, terror, and arrow
Angels to guard you in all your ways
God's promise to the one who loves him

verses.t: He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High will abide in the shadow of the Almighty.
I will say to the LORD, “You are my refuge and my fortress, my God, in whom I trust.”
Surely He will deliver you from the snare of the fowler, and from the deadly plague.
He will cover you with His feathers; under His wings you will find refuge; His faithfulness is a shield and rampart.
You will not fear the terror of the night, nor the arrow that flies by day,
nor the pestilence that stalks in the darkness, nor the calamity that destroys at noon.
Though a thousand may fall at your side, and ten thousand at your right hand, no harm will come near you.
You will only see it with your eyes and witness the punishment of the wicked.
Because you have made the LORD your dwelling— my refuge, the Most High—
no evil will befall you, no plague will approach your tent.
For He will command His angels concerning you to guard you in all your ways.
They will lift you up in their hands, so that you will not strike your foot against a stone.
You will tread on the lion and cobra; you will trample the young lion and serpent.
“Because he loves Me, I will deliver him; because he knows My name, I will protect him.
When he calls out to Me, I will answer him; I will be with him in trouble. I will deliver him and honor him.
With long life I will satisfy him and show him My salvation.”
